channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: olio e-zine — Truth · Aesthetic Revolt Art
item.description: The first issue of olio, a new e-zine put together by the visual artist Marie Magnetic, who runs it under the name Aesthetic Revolt Art. The theme is “truth”, and the brief is deliberately wide open: the call is for “all mediums that can be digitally published”, which takes in photography alongside everything else that survives a screen. Entry is free and each artist may submit one piece, as a JPG or PNG up to 50MB. Three things are worth knowing before you spend time on it. First, this is issue one — there is no back catalogue to judge the editing or production against, so you are submitting to an unproven publication; the upside is that it costs nothing but the picture. Second, the organiser's own website carries no page for this call: the terms above come from the call record she publishes on EntryThingy, and work is accepted only through a Google Form, which is sign-in gated and so requires a Google account to fill in. Third, nothing is published about rights — the call record sets out no licence, credit or usage terms, and the form itself cannot be read without signing in — so that is worth asking about before you send work. What a contributor gets is publication in the issue; no fee, payment or prize is mentioned anywhere. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Surreal Salon 19 · Baton Rouge Gallery
item.description: The nineteenth edition of Baton Rouge Gallery's annual international exhibition celebrating pop-surrealism and lowbrow art, held in partnership with the LSU School of Art and open to artists over 18 anywhere in the world. The guest juror is Lauren YS, who hand-picks the show through a blind process — the juror sees neither the artist's name nor their home city. Judging criteria are stated as conceptual and aesthetic quality, feasibility of display, and overall artistic merit. Photography is not listed among accepted media because no media list is published; what the gallery does say is that “for more than a decade, Surreal Salon has featured paintings, photography, ceramics, textiles, mixed media works, and more.” Work must be physical, tangible and non-perishable, and two-dimensional work must arrive ready to hang in a professional gallery — no bull clips, clip frames, magnets, push-pins or poster frames. $2,000 in cash prizes is awarded: $1,000 Best in Show, $600 second, $400 third. The gallery states in one place that the Best in Show artist is profiled in an online editorial by Beautiful Bizarre Magazine and in another that the editorial runs on juxtapoz.com; the two sentences sit in the same document, so expect one of them. Entry is $35 for up to three works. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 50% commission on anything sold, which is steep and worth pricing for. Selected work is delivered by 6pm on December 19, 2026; the show runs January 2 to 24, 2027 at the gallery on Dalrymple Drive, and shipping both ways is the artist's cost. Work left uncollected after February 14, 2027 is charged $10 a day in storage. The gallery reserves the right to disqualify submissions it deems pornographic, explicitly violent, obscene or hateful. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 / $600 / $400 cash + exhibition.

item.title: Lay of the Land: A Focus in Nature · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Artlink's juried group exhibition of work exploring the natural world, open to any artist 18 or over living in the United States. The gallery asks for artworks that engage the natural world through subject matter or materials — realistic depictions of flora and fauna, abstract interpretations of geological textures, or, in its own phrase, “the complex, evolving dialogue between humanity and the environment.” The call is explicit that it is open to all media, and it names photography and video alongside painting, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, installation, fiber, assemblage and drawing. There is no size limit. Entry is $12 per work with a limit of ten entries, submitted online only; jury notifications go out after November 16, 2026, accepted work is delivered by December 13, 2026, and the show runs January 7 to February 7, 2027 at the gallery. Artlink is a 501(c)3 nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. Accepted work must arrive ready to install and professionally presented. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: $12 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Adhesive Resistance · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery's virtual juried exhibition of printed matter, open to women and non-binary artists worldwide. The call names stickers, zines, pins, buttons and other printed matter, and asks for work that embraces “experimentation, cultural commentary, humor, urgency, and the democratic spirit of DIY publishing” — polished work and beautiful roughness alike. Sticker designs may be submitted as single designs or as sheets. Photography is not named as a medium either way: what the call enumerates is object types rather than media, so a photographer's route in is the printed object — a photo zine, a sticker sheet, a small-format multiple — rather than a print on a wall. The exhibition is hosted on the gallery's own website from February 27 to March 27, 2027 and promoted across its social channels. Artists in the Chicagoland area who are selected are also invited to take part in an optional in-person pop-up print fair at the gallery, and may propose workshops or demos for in-gallery programming alongside the virtual show — those proposals, if accepted, are paid. Entries are due December 31, 2026 at 11:00 PM CST, with notification January 31, 2027. The juror is Courtney Nzeribe, a Chicago-based interdisciplinary artist and writer working across fiber, painting, printmaking, collage and mixed media, who sits on the gallery's board. The entry fee is $20 — lower than the $30 on the gallery's two other current calls and the $35 of its general terms. Woman Made offers around 30 fee waivers per juried exhibition, 15 of them reserved for ALAANA/BIPOC and/or LGBTQIA+ artists, granted on a rolling basis for financial instability or low-income status, student or recent-graduate status, or other demonstrated need; members at the Enhanced Artist level and above receive one free entry a year. The gallery welcomes art from all women, including trans women and femme/feminine-identifying genderqueer and non-binary artists. Work previously shown at Woman Made cannot be resubmitted. Submitted work must be original, created by the artist, and produced without the primary use of AI image-generation tools. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Virtual exhibition.

item.title: Cedarhurst High School Art Competition 2027
item.description: Two juried competitions for high school students, run together by Cedarhurst Center for the Arts, an AAM-accredited museum and sculpture park in Mount Vernon, Illinois. Selected work hangs in the New Semantics Gallery of the Mitchell Museum, January 24 to March 21, 2027. The Cedarhurst High School Art Competition is open to students in grades 9 to 12; the Cedarhurst Administrative Counselors Art Scholarship is a separate competition for graduating seniors, for a one-year college scholarship of $2,000 contingent on the student's formal acceptance to a university. Seniors may enter both. Eligibility is also geographic — 28 named counties: Alexander, Clay, Clinton, Edwards, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Jackson, Jefferson, Johnson, Lawrence, Marion, Massac, Monroe, Perry, Pope, Pulaski, Randolph, Richland, Saline, St Clair, Union, Wabash, Washington, Wayne, White and Williamson. The call page words this as students in those counties, the registration form as high schools in them. The accepted-media list names “painting (oil, acrylic, watercolor), drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photograph (digital or film), pastels, textiles, ceramics, glass, metal, and wood”, with no installations; work must be original, and the organisers reserve the right to disqualify AI-generated images or work that violates copyright. Entry is normally school-mediated: a teacher registers the school, is emailed a shared Google folder and sheet for uploading JPEGs, may enter up to 25 artworks with a limit of 3 per student, and is invoiced $3 per artwork once the window closes. Seniors submit one portfolio of six works for $10. Home-school students, and anyone who wants to enter without a registered teacher, are told on the call page to contact the competition's organiser directly. Awards total more than $3,000 and are chosen after the work is delivered: the $2,000 scholarship, $200 Best of Show, $100 / $75 / $50 for first, second and third in both Best of Two-Dimensional and Best of Three-Dimensional Art, and twenty honorable mentions of $25 each. Accepted work is emailed to registered teachers by the end of December 18, 2026 and must reach the Mitchell Museum by Friday January 15, 2027; it cannot be removed before the exhibit closes, and is collected March 23 to April 2, 2027. The organiser's two surfaces disagree on the deadline and the earlier is stored: the call page requires uploads by 5pm December 2, 2026, the registration form says artwork must be registered by December 3, 2026. — Deadline: December 2, 2026. Fee: $3 per artwork ($10 per senior portfolio). Prize: $2,000 scholarship + Exhibition.

item.title: Assignment Literary Magazine — 2026 Winter Issue: Visual Art
item.description: Free visual-art submissions for the Winter 2026 issue of Assignment, the literary magazine run by Southern New Hampshire University's Master of Fine Arts in Fiction or Nonfiction program. Art is considered for the front and back covers of the issue as well as for internal use; artists may submit up to five pieces per submission, formatted one piece per page, as high-resolution images. Review is blind — the guidelines ask that no name or identifying information appear on the submission. Simultaneous submissions are accepted provided the editors are told if work is placed elsewhere, and everything submitted must be original and previously unpublished. The magazine publishes using First North American Serial Rights, after which all rights revert to the author, and states that none of its content is available for use by AI. Submitted work must be the artist's own with no AI used in its creation — a line that appears in the guidelines and again on every one of the four entry-form categories. The submission window for the issue closes November 15, 2026, across all four categories (visual art, poetry, fiction and non-fiction), and the entry route is Submittable with no fee on any category. Two things to weigh: the call asks for "visual art" and nowhere enumerates the media it accepts, so photography is not named either way — what settles it is the magazine's own record. Its online-only section ran a photographic essay, "Through Mami’s Eyes", a visual diary of the artist’s mother through the Covid-19 pandemic by Gabrielle Ghzala LaGuerre, described there as "a photo-based artist whose work explores people in their natural environments", and its Featured Artwork posts carried Guilherme Bergamini, a "Reporter photographic and visual artist" who "has developed projects with photography" — both in 2023, which is where that section stops. Neither the guidelines nor the entry form mentions payment; the stated return is publication. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Alternatives 2027 — Identity Fractured · Ohio University School of Art + Design
item.description: The 2027 edition of Alternatives, the photography biennial that Ohio University's MFA Photography + Integrated Media programme has run out of The School of Art + Design since 1980. The organisers describe it as "a long running biennial juried exhibition" that has "achieved national recognition for its leadership in forging new definitions in the medium by emphasizing the work of photographers in the conceptual forefront of the practice", and its money comes from an unusual endowment — the legacies of Clarence White, founder of the Clarence White School of Photography in New York, and his son Clarence White Jr., who re-established the school at Ohio University in 1948 and created what the programme calls the first degree-granting photography programme at a major university in the country. Past jurors named by the organisers are Carrie Mae Weems, Duane Michals, Kelli Connell, Jason Reed, Judy Natal and, most recently, Willie Osterman; the 2027 juror is Dan Estabrook. This cycle's theme is Identity Fractured: "Photography is a medium that has the power to capture, preserve, change, and distort history, places, and people. Using this medium we can tell stories about ourselves and others, play pretend, or show real pieces of ourselves... We are taking and analyzing parts of ourselves within every frame. Whether it is self portraiture, photographing others, or even objects. We all place ourselves into an image one way or another." Each artist may submit five files at 10 MB each for a flat $35, through a Google Form that requires a Google account to open. The programme gives its own address as the Ohio University Art Gallery in Athens; the 2027 call itself names no venue. Two disclosures: the School of Art + Design's own Alternatives page had not been updated at the time of listing and still carries the 2025 edition ("Image as Record", juried by Willie Osterman), so the 2027 call lives on the programme's own Instagram and on the submission form; and while previous editions were billed as an international biennial, the 2027 poster reads "A National Photography Biennial" — no residency or nationality rule is published on either surface. Neither readable surface announces a notification date, prize money or exhibition dates, and the entry form is sign-in gated, so it could not be read. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 ArtFields Competition & Festival
item.description: ArtFields turns the whole of Lake City, South Carolina into a gallery for seventeen days each spring, and its signature visual-art competition is open for the 2027 edition — the festival's 15th year. Work is not hung on white walls: selected pieces go up in "galleries, warehouses, restaurants, shops, and other venues throughout downtown," so that, as ArtFields puts it, art is met "from grabbing their cup of morning coffee to getting a haircut." An average of 400 works are invited from the submissions, rated 1–10 by an independent panel of arts professionals through the ArtBooth platform. Photography is unambiguously in: the competition rules say "Artists may submit one 2-D or 3-D artwork in any visual art medium," and the entry portal repeats that the competition "is open to artists of all media." The prize pool is over $100,000 — a $50,000 Grand Prize and a $25,000 Second Place chosen by the jury panel, two $12,500 People's Choice Awards (one 2-D, one 3-D) decided by public vote, five $2,000 Merit Awards, and Southeastern Partnership Awards of exhibitions and opportunities. An artist may win only one of the top four. The entry is $25 for a single work; you may upload up to five images of that one work, and submitting a portfolio of separate pieces is grounds for disqualification. Eligibility is regional and strict: you must have lived in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or West Virginia for at least six consecutive months before submitting, be 18 or older, and the work must have been completed in or after 2024. Work shown at a previous ArtFields is not eligible, and last year's top-four winners sit out a cycle. Submissions close 11:59 p.m. EDT on Sunday, November 1, 2026; invitations and declines go out by Wednesday, December 9, 2026; venue invitations follow by January 29, 2027 and the signed Artist & Venue Hosting Agreement is due February 5. Work must reach Lake City between March 5 and 13, 2027 (installations by March 20) and stay up for the festival, 9 April – 1 May 2027; artists other than installation-makers need not travel, as trained handlers install at each venue. Costs to weigh: you pay transport both ways and insure the work yourself, return shipping requires a prepaid label packed with the piece, and venues take 20% of any sale. Work is sold at the artist's discretion, and top-four winners agree to leave the awarded piece with ArtFields / the Lake City Creative Alliance for a further 90-day public exhibition, during which ArtFields has an option — not an obligation — to acquire it for its permanent collection, with the cash award as the full and only consideration. One technical rule worth reading twice: work "deemed not ready to hang or show as delivered will be excluded," so D-rings and wiring matter. ArtFields also bars anything "created solely through Artificial Intelligence (AI) software." — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $50,000 Grand Prize + $25,000 Second Place + $12,500 People's Choice + 5 x $2,000 Merit Awards.

item.title: Future Visions · Kunsthalle Luzern
item.description: Kunsthalle Luzern and the akku Kunstplattform in Emmenbrücke have launched a Switzerland-wide open call on a single question: what does the future look like from here? "The future is not a place we wait for," the call opens. "It takes shape in the images, conflicts and decisions of the present." The two institutions are after work that engages social, technological, ecological or political transformation and builds an independent position out of it — "conceptual, speculative, poetic, critical or experimental approaches from all areas of contemporary" art. It is free to enter and open to artists resident in Switzerland, individuals and collectives alike, from students to established practitioners; existing works and newly planned projects are equally welcome, provided a proposal is "technically and spatially feasible" within what the two spaces can do. Submit at least one and at most three proposed works, each with title, year, material, dimensions and up to five images (video as a link plus a still — no uploaded files), all inside one PDF of 10 MB or less named Surname_Firstname_FV2027.pdf. You cannot apply to just one of the two venues: a single proposal may be assigned to only one of them, but different proposals from the same practice can go to both, and site-specific proposals are the one exception, provided the tie to that space is argued in the application. Selection is by the curatorial teams of both institutions together with three external experts — Katrin Sperry, Michel Rebosura and Sebastian Utzni — on artistic and conceptual quality, thematic relevance, willingness to experiment, and feasibility. Two separate exhibitions follow: Kunsthalle Luzern 4 July – 19 September 2027 (opening Saturday 3 July), akku Kunstplattform 11 July – 5 September 2027 (opening Saturday 10 July). On money, the institutions commit in writing: "The Kunsthalle Luzern and the akku Kunstplattform are committed to fair fees and good working conditions for artists. Exhibition fees are based on the visarte recommendations applicable to smaller institutions," with further contributions towards production costs possible in justified cases from the project budget — no figure is published. Artists pay transport and return themselves; the institutions insure the work from receipt through dismantling, and artists supply their own monitors, projectors and playback equipment for media works. Applications go only through the form on the Kunsthalle Luzern project page — nothing else is accepted — and close Sunday 15 November 2026, with jury feedback by Monday 14 December 2026. The project was conceived by Marius Geschinske, director of the Kunsthalle Luzern. Neither the project page nor the six-page open-call dossier names a medium list beyond "all areas of contemporary art"; the Kunsthalle's group show *Crossroad – Home in Motion* (4 July – 27 September 2026) put photographers among its sixteen positions — Hans U. Alder, whose own site is fotografiealder.com, and Mischa Christen, "a Swiss photographer based in Lucerne". — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Artist fee.

item.title: Fins, Feathers, and Fur · St. Charles Arts Council
item.description: "Beyond the surface of animal portraiture lies a rich world of pattern, rhythm, and tactile wonder." The St. Charles Arts Council's juried autumn show asks for work that investigates the physical and visual surfaces of the animal kingdom — "literal representations, or abstract explorations" — under the subtitle *Textures of the Living World*. It hangs in the council's SCAC Gallery at 121 2nd Street in historic downtown St. Charles, Illinois, from 30 October to 20 December 2026, with awards handed out at the opening reception on Friday 30 October, 5–7pm. All media are accepted — the organiser says so twice, "All mediums are accepted, 3d encouraged" and "All forms of media accepted" — so photographs compete alongside everything else; the judge is Chris Hughes, an award-winning member of Oil Painters of America who sits on the boards of the Naperville Art League and the DuPage Art League and teaches at both. Awards are Best in Show $150, second place $75, third place $50, plus honourable mentions at the judge's discretion. Entry is $35 for non-members and $20 for SCAC members, selected from a drop-down at checkout, and one entry covers up to two pieces; only one entry per artist. Work must be original, created within the last five years, and must not have been shown in any previous SCAC exhibit. Everything must be for sale — the council is explicit that the "NFS" option in the entry form must not be selected — and sales split 60% to the artist, 40% to the council. Two practical constraints before you enter: all work must be wired to hang, with sawtooth hangers refused, and you must be able to make the in-person dates yourself, drop-off Monday 26 October 2–6pm and collection Monday 21 December 2–6pm, which effectively limits this to artists who can get to St. Charles twice. Two clauses of the artist contract are worth reading before you pay: all artists with work in the show "are asked to sign up to volunteer at The ARC" on two-hour shifts, and any work not claimed within seven days of the pick-up date, without notice, "becomes the property of the St. Charles Arts Council". Entries close 11 October 2026 and the jury decision is posted 14 October. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $35 non-members / $20 SCAC members. Prize: $150 / $75 / $50 + Exhibition.

item.title: Embodied Existence · Chronic Pain Project
item.description: The Chronic Pain Project is a 501(c)(3) built on a simple premise — "Chronic pain is invisible. We can change that" — that brings artists living with chronic pain together so their work can do the explaining. Its next exhibition, *Embodied Existence*, asks what it means to be embodied while living with chronic pain, and it hangs at the Watzek Library on the Lewis & Clark College campus in Portland from 9 October to 6 November 2026. Entry is free and the bar is deliberately low: "Art depicting the experience of living with chronic pain. That's it. No specific medium, style, or approach required. Just your truth, told your way." All skill levels are welcome — "You don't need formal training or a gallery resume" — 2D and 3D work are both encouraged, though display space for 3D is limited, and photography sits comfortably inside that. There is a content screen, though: the project does not accept explicit content — "Keep it PG-13 - no drugs, sex, alcohol" — and work "will be turned away if it contains discriminatory themes and gratuitous violence", which is worth weighing if your account of chronic pain runs through medication. Who may enter: anyone 18 or over who lives with chronic pain, or who cares for someone who does. Caregivers are actively wanted and the definition is broad — healthcare providers, family, friends, community members — with the one condition that a caregiver's submission be health-related in some way. The call is local by design: only work that can be dropped off on 8 October and collected on 9 November at the Lewis & Clark campus is accepted, so this is for the Portland metropolitan area. Two submissions per artist are allowed and roughly 10–15 further pieces will fit in the show, so both may not be taken. Work must arrive exhibition-ready and installation-ready — hanging hardware attached, since "work that arrives without proper installation hardware cannot be included" — and the project handles installation at the venue. Nothing is insured: the terms warn that work "may be installed in high-traffic locations or other places with public access and little or no supervision" with "minor theft deterrent elements", and that neither the project nor the exhibition site carries coverage against damage, destruction or theft, so that risk stays with the artist. You upload at least two good photographs of the piece and a short statement; submit through Artwork Archive and also complete the project's Google Form, since both are required. Work will be for sale at the exhibition and in the project's online gallery, with the artist keeping 75% and the project 25%. Artists are optionally invited to record a video about the work for the project's artist-interview series. The deadline is Friday 2 October 2026 and acceptances are confirmed by 6 October. One inconsistency to note: the project's own Upcoming Events page lists the Watzek Library exhibit as running 5 October 2026 – 5 January 2027, while the call document and the entry platform both say 9 October – 6 November; the call's own dates are used here. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Yéego Action Grant · First Peoples Fund
item.description: First Peoples Fund's Yéego Action Grant exists for the moment a working artist needs money quickly and there is no cycle to wait for. It offers $100 to $2,500 to individual Native artists and culture bearers who need "financial assistance with a specific professional opportunity or towards a hardship that is hindering their creative practice." The name carries the Diné word *yéego*, a phrase of encouragement that can mean "keep going" or "don't give up." The eligible uses are concrete and unusually practical: entry or workshop fees to take up an art opportunity; travel, lodging and meals to attend a residency, seminar or similar professional development; expenses from an emergency such as fire, theft or a natural disaster; repair of damaged equipment or tools; unanticipated transport needs, from a vehicle repair to a bus pass; unexpected medical or health costs that stop you working; and sudden unforeseen expenses on a current project, such as replacing damaged supplies or finding a new venue. What it will not do is equally clear — no reimbursement for money already spent, no general purchases of new tools, materials or equipment, no tuition or student loans, no organisational operating support, and no funding for new or existing projects, exhibitions or programming. Applicants must be at least 18, must be enrolled members of or provide proof of lineal descent from a US federally or state-recognised tribe, or proof of Alaska Native or Native Hawaiian ancestry, must be practising artists, must not be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme, and must not have received a Yéego grant before; current FPF grantees, fellows and leaders of grantees are ineligible, and group or multiple-artist requests are not considered. The Submittable application adds one bar the programme page omits: an applicant "must be a U.S. based resident". There is no fee. Applications run through Submittable and ask for three recent examples of your work with a brief description of each, used to confirm you are a practising artist; a website or social link is optional and explicitly does not affect scoring, because FPF "recognise[s] that not everyone maintains an online presence." Supporting links and up to two documents — an invoice, a quote, a budget — are also optional. The grant runs on a monthly rhythm: the portal normally opens by the 12th, the deadline is the 10th of every month at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time, applicants hear by the last day of the month, and approved funds arrive roughly six to eight weeks after the monthly due date. The round open at the time of writing closes Saturday 10 October 2026. FPF staff and leadership review the applications. One thing to know before applying: the fund is open to artists of every discipline and First Peoples Fund's own pages enumerate no list of accepted media, so nothing here is specific to photography — but nothing excludes it either, and camera repair and market entry fees are named uses. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $100–$2,500.

item.title: Visual Art Open Call · The Closed Eye Open
item.description: The Closed Eye Open is a small art-and-literature journal — its current issue is Issue XV — that describes itself as "an exploration of the many forms of self-expression" and sets out to publish work "that may not necessarily connect with other publications" — "Pieces that are weird, unconventional, or even experimental may very well fit with what we're going for." Its visual-art call is open for upcoming issues, and photography is named in the accepted forms: "Visual art may include painting, drawing, photography & print-making, digital art, and hybrid forms." Submit up to six pieces as JPEGs at whatever file size suits you — higher resolution is requested later if a piece is taken — with a statement or cover letter, a short third-person bio, links, and optionally a title list as you want it to appear. Each piece is generally viewed individually, so a submission may deliberately vary in style and subject; if you would rather it be read as one body of work, say so in the cover letter. Simultaneous submissions are accepted on the condition that you withdraw anything placed elsewhere, and work posted only on your own website, blog or social account does not count as previously published. Rights are light-touch: acceptance grants the journal online publishing and archival rights, and after publication all rights revert to the artist, with a request for a credit if the work appears elsewhere later. Issues come out online as PDFs, two or three a year, alongside an ongoing *Maya's Micros* feature updated roughly twice a month. The editors invite people from outside the art world as much as inside — "from established writers & artists, to those in academic disciplines, to those who may be new to the world of sharing their work with a larger audience" — and say a scientific, spiritual or liberal-arts starting point is equally welcome. Submissions run through Submittable and carry a $4.50 fee; the visual-art category closes 30 September 2026. No payment to contributors is mentioned and the journal names no notification date. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $4.50. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Guest Room: Sofia Krysiak & Jack Latham · Der Greif
item.description: The next edition of Der Greif's monthly Guest Room, the Munich non-profit's online exhibition format in which an invited figure from contemporary photography curates an open submission in real time. This round is curated by Sofia Krysiak and Jack Latham, co-founders of the Nashville photobook publisher Terrible Baby, under the theme "Difficult Conversations". Their brief opens on a question — "Some conversations are difficult to have, so, how do we have them?" — and asks for work that opens up social, political or personal realities and "stories that refuse to be avoided and brushed under the carpet". The curators are explicit that photographs do not simply make hard subjects legible: images "can expose and conceal, humanise and stereotype, complicate and flatten", and the same photograph produces radically different readings depending on who is looking, who made it and where it circulates. At a moment when disagreement increasingly impedes conversation and information proliferates faster than its veracity can be gauged, they ask whether visual language can help us have the conversations we need to have. A submission is one project of one to five photographs; video works are also accepted, up to ten minutes, and if selected the full video is published on Der Greif's site with excerpts on its social channels. Entry is free — Der Greif is a registered non-profit and suggests a voluntary €5 or €10 donation, with a 50 or 100 percent discount code available by email to anyone unable to contribute. Images already selected for a past Der Greif opportunity may not be resubmitted. Selected work is published in an online showcase alongside emerging artists worldwide, and the selected photographers get an online feedback session with the curators. Krysiak is a publisher, curator, writer and photography researcher, originally from Buenos Aires and now based in Nashville, who directs Terrible Baby and co-founded HER Photo Agency; Latham is a Welsh photographer and publisher, an Associate Professor of Photography at Belmont University, whose work sits between photojournalism and conceptual art and questions the mechanisms of disinformation. The Guest Room goes live on dergreif.org on 20 November 2026. — Deadline: October 28, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €5 or €10 donation). Prize: Publication + portfolio feedback.

item.title: 2027 Artist Residencies · Djerassi Resident Artists Program
item.description: The Djerassi Resident Artists Program's 2027 season, on a 583-acre ranch in the Santa Cruz Mountains above Woodside, California, where the programme has given more than 2,700 writers, visual and media artists, composers, choreographers, filmmakers and scientists a month of time and space across 43 years — "all at no cost to the artists". Applicants pick one category per cycle, and Visual Arts is defined as "Painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, mixed media, and installation"; the programme's own 2027 details PDF credits its illustrations to "Film photography by Jessie Barr, 2025 Djerassi Program Alumnus". Five one-month sessions run from mid-February to mid-November 2027 — 16 February to 16 March, 30 March to 27 April, 22 June to 27 July (the Leonardo@Djerassi cohort of five artists and five scientists, with Leonardo/ISAST, which includes public forums, a feature in LEONARDO from MIT Press and open studios), 17 August to 14 September, and 19 October to 16 November — and the programme anticipates accommodating around 40 to 45 new artists. Each resident gets a private live/work studio with a workspace suited to their discipline, chef-prepared weeknight dinners with kitchens stocked for the rest, laundry, SFO pickup and return and local transport during the stay, and 583 acres of trails, redwoods and site-specific sculpture; artists pay their own way to the Bay Area. It is open to national and international applicants at every career stage, eligibility has recently been expanded to include degree-seeking students, alumni must wait five seasons before reapplying, and all materials must be in English. No accommodation is available for partners, children or pets, and residents commit to the whole session — there are no partial residencies. Apply through SlideRoom with a statement of interest, descriptions of two recent projects, a CV, one to five work samples (visual artists upload up to five JPEGs), your website and Instagram, and ranked session preferences. The application fee is $35. Staff screen for completeness, then a jury of artists and arts professionals scores merit of past work, readiness to engage with a month of uninterrupted time, and potential for impact; all applicants are tentatively notified by 31 December 2026. Applications opened 1 September and close 9 October 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: One-month residency.

item.title: 2027 AIM Fellowship · The Bronx Museum
item.description: The 47th cycle of the AIM Fellowship, The Bronx Museum's career accelerator for emerging artists based in New York City, founded in 1980 as Artist in the Marketplace. Fourteen artists are selected each year through open competition for a nine-month practicum of expert-led seminars at the museum: the art market, the artist statement, community building, communication strategies, the curator/artist relationship, financial literacy, funding opportunities and art law in the first half; studio visits, portfolio reviews, peer-led sessions, guest artist visits, career planning, exhibition preparation and time management, working with institutions big and small, audience development, community art practice, artist archives and documentation in the second. Fellows meet on Tuesday evenings, 6 to 9pm, at the museum from February to June 2027, break for July and August, and resume from September to December; the cohort then designs and co-facilitates a mandatory public AIM Convening in winter or spring 2028, and a group exhibition with a fully illustrated catalogue follows roughly every two years. There is no application fee and no cost to participate. AIM has helped more than 1,300 New York artists establish careers, among them Njideka Akunyili-Crosby, Glenn Ligon, Abigail DeVille, Byron Kim, Lucia Hierro, Jacolby Satterwhite and the photographer LaToya Ruby Frazier — the call names no accepted-media list at all, and that alumni roster is where the question of photography is answered. Eligibility is specific: at least 21; applying as an individual, not a partnership or collective; an emerging artist with two to ten years actively creating and presenting new original work in the visual arts who has yet to be substantially celebrated; a New York City resident at application and throughout the term; not enrolled in a degree-granting programme or another professional-development programme during the fellowship; not a Bronx Museum employee or a board member's relative; and not represented by a commercial gallery anywhere in or outside the US. Because stipends, honoraria and wage payments are involved, enrolment is limited to US citizens and permanent residents. Apply through Submittable with six works no more than three years old; semi-finalists must be available for an in-person group interview with the selection committee at the museum in autumn 2026. The museum is explicit that this is not a studio programme and that no studio space is provided. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fellowship.

item.title: Art x Newlab Creative Residency 2027 · Michigan Central
item.description: The fourth year of the Michigan Central Art x Newlab Creative Residency, a twelve-week research-based fellowship in Detroit's innovation district run in partnership with Newlab and Henry Ford Health with funds from the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. Fellows are selected across two tracks: Art & Tech, with Newlab and Knight Foundation support, for practices at the edge of technology, data visualisation, wearable tech, accessibility and sustainability; and Art & Health, with Henry Ford Health, for artists working across wellness, care and health technology. Each fellow-in-residence receives a $30,000 prize to advance their project, access to Newlab Detroit's fabrication shops and to facilities across Michigan Central and Henry Ford Health, project-aligned research opportunities, a place in a public conversation series, and external mentors who both support the selection review and give ongoing guidance. Two sessions frame the on-site time and applicants rank a preference: 8 February to 30 April 2027, and 17 May to 6 August 2027. Michigan Central's art-programme page describes the residency as foregrounding emerging and mid-career artists based primarily in metro Detroit, and the form asks whether you are a current resident of south-eastern Michigan, but the call invites artists, creatives, researchers and makers "across disciplines and geographies"; the stated requirements are to be over 25, to apply as a single person or entity rather than a group or collaboration, and to be eligible to receive taxable income via an SSN, ITIN or EIN. Photography is one of the seven categories the organiser lists on its own Artwork Archive posting, alongside craft, drawing, film/video/new media, mixed media, painting and sculpture. Applying is free through Michigan Central's Submittable and the organiser has deliberately shortened it, suggesting no more than five hours in total: a project title, a one-sentence and a two-paragraph description with goals, community engagement and expected outcomes, a focus-area paragraph, a needs paragraph on equipment and technical assistance, a high-level budget for the $30,000, and up to five work samples with credit lines. A panel of experts across art, technology and health scores clarity and originality of the idea, alignment with the track themes, feasibility within twelve weeks, and potential for impact and innovation. Past fellows-in-residence include Simon Anton, Ash Arder, Michael Candy, Osman Khan, Salam Rida, Wes Taylor, Sabrina Nelson and Chloe Pascal Crawford. A virtual open house runs on 8 October 2026, and accessibility needs can be raised with the residency team. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30,000 + Residency.

item.title: 2026 Velocity Fund Project Grants
item.description: The Velocity Fund's 2026 cycle, open from 22 September to 22 November 2026, giving Philadelphia-based artists project grants of $5,000 each. It is one of 41 Regional Regranting Programs of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, hosted by Asian Arts Initiative in Philadelphia's Chinatown North after earlier stints at Philadelphia Contemporary and at Temple Contemporary in the Tyler School of Art and Architecture; the Foundation set the programme up in 2007 to reach independently organised, public-facing, artist-centred activity that animates local art scenes but lies beyond the reach of traditional funding. Applying is free — "There is no application fee to apply." Individual artists living in Philadelphia may apply, as may artist-run spaces and collectives whose lead applicant lives in Philadelphia; incorporated 501(c)(3) nonprofits, for-profit businesses, artists living outside Philadelphia, senior Asian Arts Initiative staff and any lead applicant who received a Velocity grant the previous year may not. The project must involve visual arts components, take place between February 2027 and February 2028, and reach a public outcome in Philadelphia inside that window. The fund will not reimburse or resolve work already underway, and says plainly that applications only for travel, studio rent or equipment, with no public outcome, are not encouraged; it favours projects rooted in their communities, led by artists, mindful of their impact, and staged in those communities rather than in commercial galleries and museums. The fund defines what it supports as work using visual arts "including (but never limited to) printmaking, performance, video, puppetry, sculpture, and curation" — photography is not on that list and does not need to be, since the most recent cohort includes Uriah Bussey's Disabling the Queer Lens, a film and digital photography series of Black and Brown queer disabled people made with COVID-safer portraits, ending in a photobook, cyanotype prints and a public exhibition. Apply through Submittable with a biography of the lead applicant and collaborators, a description of your audience, a description of the visual arts involved, a project proposal in writing or on video, a timeline, the fund's budget form and five to ten work samples; a lead applicant may submit one proposal per cycle, and may reuse last year's application because each year has a new panel. That panel is independent of Velocity, Asian Arts Initiative and Warhol Foundation staff, includes one former grantee and one administrator from another Regional Regranting Program, scores on artistic vision, connection to publics, capacity to realise the project and personal impact, then meets over the 30 top-scoring applications to choose the final 12 to 14 grantees; the panellists are named after the awards are made. Grantees are notified in early February 2027 and receive 80 percent of the money up front, the rest after a midterm check-in. Applications are also offered in Vietnamese. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 (12–14 grants).

item.title: 40th Annual Sears Invitational Art Show & Sale · Sears Art Museum
item.description: The 40th Annual Sears Invitational Art Show & Sale at the Sears Art Museum, Utah Tech University in St. George — the museum's premier event, founded by Robert N. Sears (1915–1995), a retired vice-president of Phillips Petroleum who worked to establish a quality art invitational at the university, and now one of Utah's longest-running and most popular juried museum exhibitions. Around 100 artists and roughly 200 works are selected by jury for a six-week run, 13 February to 27 March 2027, opening with a gala on 12 February. Entry is free: "There is no fee to enter!" The museum answers the media question outright in its own FAQ — "We welcome visual art of all subjects and mediums—including watercolor, oil, acrylic, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, photography, mixed media, 2D digital art, and more." Any artist aged 18 or older based in the western United States may submit, with priority given to artists from Utah, Idaho, Colorado and Nevada. You may submit up to three individual pieces, each as a separate ArtCall entry and each editable until the call closes, and a maximum of two will be accepted; recent work is asked for and everything submitted must be available for sale. Each entry needs a high-quality image, the title, dimensions, sale price and medium, your location and a brief artist bio. Selected artists are included in a professionally designed full-colour exhibition catalogue available for purchase by museum patrons, and gain the show's audience of collectors, curators, visitors and fellow artists. Sales split 60 percent to the artist and 40 percent to the museum, which funds exhibitions, educational programmes and part-time student positions, and the museum's share is tax-deductible for the buyer. Local artists drop off and collect in St. George, and the museum runs a complimentary van service to and from Ogden, Salt Lake City and Orem; artists outside Utah, or unable to use those points, are responsible for round-trip shipping. Acceptances are posted at searsart.com and emailed on 16 November 2026. One caution: one FAQ answer dates the run "February 13 through March 27, 2026" while the call's own timeline block and the ArtCall prospectus both say 2027 — the exhibition is in 2027. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Young Photographer Awards 2026 · Photo Museum Ireland
item.description: Photo Museum Ireland, the national centre for contemporary photography, runs the Young Photographer Awards as its national photography awards for young people, and the 2026 edition is open to anyone aged 8 to 18 living on the island of Ireland. The museum's own terms scope it to young people resident in the Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland who were aged between 8 and 18 inclusive on 31 December 2025 — born between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2017 — and entries are judged separately in two age groups, 8–13 and 14–18. Entry is free, each entrant may submit up to ten photographs, and the museum is explicit that no previous experience or specialist equipment is needed: photographs made with a phone, a digital camera, an analogue camera or another photographic process are all accepted. Judging is on three equally weighted criteria — strength of the idea, creativity and originality, and visual impact — with the photographer's age taken into account; judges see the photographs, titles and age group only, not names or contact details. One overall Young Photographer of the Year is selected from the six age-category winners, with three Rising Stars winners drawn from the 8–13 group, three from the 14–18 group, and a wider shortlist of Highly Commended photographers. Winning and shortlisted photographs go into a large-scale public outdoor exhibition on Admiral Browne Walk at Sir John Rogerson's Quay in Grand Canal Dock, Dublin, presented with support from IPUT and launching in late November 2026. Entrants under 16 need a parent or guardian to authorise the entry through a secure email link before it reaches the judges, and an unauthorised entry is deleted after seven days. Images containing elements produced or modified with artificial intelligence must be identified and categorised as such at entry, and entrants must not present AI-generated material as wholly their own photographic work. Submissions open on Monday 31 August 2026 and close at 11pm on Sunday 11 October 2026, Irish time, through the museum's CameraComp entry portal. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rawhead: Point Blank — Semi-monthly Digital Series
item.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of poetry, fiction, nonfiction and visual art that reads the arts as a form of resistance, and Point Blank is its rapid-response strand: a digital series featuring the work of a single writer or artist, released semi-monthly, made in direct response to what is happening now. The editors describe it as a form of resistance and documentation — a way of marking what is being done, who it is being done to, and how it is being fought — and they name the ground explicitly: state violence, the kidnapping and murder of neighbours by ICE, the genocide of the Palestinian people, the plunder of the earth, economic hardship, legislative attacks on LGBTQ+ people and systemic racism. Just as explicitly, they want the other half of the ledger: mutual aid, community care, healing and recovery, the defence of neighbours, everyday kindness, and the art made in spite of it all. They say they want to hear from anyone paying attention, whether that perspective comes from the shop floor, the classroom, the kitchen table, the picket line, the waiting room, the cell, the back roads or the street. Photographers enter through the Visual Art category, which takes three to ten pieces in any medium and enumerates photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture; images should be at least 1500px as JPG, PNG or TIFF. Submission is free and the journal states it is committed to always offering free submissions, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that it says have no bearing on editorial decisions. Each featured contributor receives a flat $30 honorarium plus a $10 donation to a charity of their choice. Work not selected for Point Blank may still be considered for Rawhead's general issues. Simultaneous submissions are accepted and previously published work is welcome where the rights have reverted, the original publication is credited and at least six months have passed. AI-generated content is not accepted: submissions must be original, human-made and free of AI assistance. The editors aim to respond within three months. Rawhead's own submissions page describes Point Blank as an ongoing, semi-monthly series and gives no closing date; the dated surface is the Submittable category, whose header reads “Ends on Sun, Nov 1, 2026 4:00 AM” — that is the raw UTC instant, which is midnight US Eastern at the end of Saturday 31 October 2026. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30 + Publication.

item.title: Anything but…Plastic · Riverside Arts Center
item.description: Riverside Arts Center, a 501(c)(3) arts centre on Huron Street in Ypsilanti, programmes Anything but…Plastic into its 2026–27 gallery season as a group exhibition built around a single material constraint. The call opens with the dictionary definition of plastic and then throws it out: no acrylic paint or gesso, no synthetic fibres, no found objects containing plastic, no Mod Podge or plastic adhesives, no 3D printing, no plastic or acrylic beads. 'Acrylic paint? Get outta here! Try some homemade egg tempera! Nylon thread? No way!' The centre's allowed list is oil paint, watercolour, natural fibres, wood, charcoal, oil pastels, ceramics and glass, and it is explicitly non-exhaustive — 'include, but are not limited to' — with an invitation to get in touch if you are unsure about your medium. Photography is not named in either list, so read the constraint as the brief rather than as a bar: a resin-coated print is polyethylene-coated and will not clear it, and an inkjet paper with a polymer receiving layer is exactly the case the gallery asks you to raise with it, while fibre-based silver gelatin, cyanotype, platinum-palladium, salted paper and other plastic-free processes plainly can. The ban is scoped to the work itself — the prospectus adds that frames and installation materials are not included — and the gallery's concurrent exhibition Deconstruction is described in its own words as combining photography, drawing, painting and found-object art. Entry is free — the centre states on its Artist Opportunities page that all of its calls for art are always free to enter — and the call is open to artists of all ages, locally, regionally and nationally, with priority possibly given to artists based in south-eastern Michigan. Applications go through Artwork Archive, which caps a submission at three pieces; the prospectus asks for one to five high-quality images plus an artist statement of 100–300 words and a one-to-two-page bio or CV. Work must be display-ready, framed or wired, and no larger than 36 by 48 inches unless pre-approved. Work created wholly or partially with AI tools must be disclosed at submission and will then be judged on the same criteria as everything else. The gallery insures work on its premises to $5,000 a piece and takes a 30 percent commission on sales; artists deliver and collect their own work at their own cost. No juror is named and no award is offered: the gallery has final authority over inclusion, and what a selected artist gets is the exhibition itself. The call closes 9 November 2026 at 11:59pm Eastern, artists are notified on 13 November, work is dropped off on 30 November, and the exhibition runs 4 December 2026 to 10 January 2027 with an opening reception on 4 December. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 BAXTER ST Residency
item.description: Baxter St at the Camera Club of New York — one of the city's oldest not-for-profit arts organisations and a base for the contemporary lens-based community — invites emerging lens-based artists living in New York City who have yet to have a solo exhibition in the city to apply for its workspace residency. Residents get free use of Baxter St's facilities and equipment for the duration of the residency, a stipend of $1,000 a month across the three months of workspace access, a $750 materials fee towards film, printing and other production costs, a $3,000 production fee to realise the exhibition, and $165 per public programme. Each resident is granted a solo exhibition at Baxter St after their residency term, and takes part in the organisation's programming: a public conversation, a video interview and one-on-one meetings with an Art Advisory Committee member and Baxter St staff. The organisers read lens-based broadly — photographers, filmmakers, collage artists and others who use photography as a medium or a point of departure are all welcome. Applicants must be New York City residents for the duration of the residency period and 18 or older; living accommodation is not provided. Only lens-based work is considered, and Baxter St staff, board members, previous Workspace or Darkroom residents and their families are not eligible. Anyone enrolled in a degree-granting programme as of 1 January 2026 is ineligible, and students must have completed their studies on or before 1 January 2027. There is no fee to apply. The application, made through Submittable, asks for a work sample of ten images (installation shots allowed) plus up to one video of a maximum three minutes, a letter of intent of up to 300 words carrying an exhibition proposal, a one-paragraph artist statement of up to 300 words, a one-page CV and two references. The 2027 application cycle opened on 23 September 2026 and closes 25 November 2026 at 11:59pm ET; Baxter St states the deadline will not be extended, and a jury of art professionals considers every eligible application. The residency is supported by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, the Joy of Giving Something, Inc., and the Howard and Sarah D. Solomon Foundation. Note on access: the ground-floor galleries and restroom at 154 Ludlow Street are wheelchair accessible, but the main resident workspace is one flight down and is not. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + $1,000/month stipend + solo exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Portrait
item.description: The SE Center's open call on the portrait, classic to contemporary. The organisers frame it around what portraits are for: objects of remembrance and reverence, of seduction and glorification — from the keepsake in a locket to the likeness of a leader meant to inspire, images that can stir and confront and drive us to action just as they can lull us into longing for a time since passed, acting as a mirror in which we find our own inward experience or as a window onto the virtues of another. Analog and digital manipulation in all its forms is welcome, monochrome or colour, any subject, analog, digital or antique processes, and photographers of every skill level and location may enter. The juror is Aline Smithson, the Los Angeles visual artist, educator and editor best known for conceptual portraiture that uses humour and pathos to explore the performative potential of photography; she has had over forty solo shows at institutions including the Griffin Museum of Photography, the Santa Barbara Museum of Art and the Center for Fine Art Photography, her work is held in public collections, and in 2007 she founded Lenscratch. Between thirty-five and forty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $35 for up to five images and $6 for each additional image to a maximum of fifteen; members pay $28 and $5. Work exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years is not eligible, and there are no refunds for images not selected. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions opened 6 September 2026 and close 15 November; selections are announced 1 December and the exhibition runs 15 December 2026 to 30 January 2027. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Members Show 2026–27
item.description: The SE Center's annual members' exhibition, open to any photographer who joins the Center. Anything goes: all subjects, any photo-based imagery, analog and digital manipulation in all its forms, monochrome or colour, analog, digital or antique processes, and member photographers of every skill level and location are welcome. The juror is Michael Pannier, an award-winning fine art and commercial photographer based in Greenville with thirty years in photography and forty-five in the gallery and art world, who founded the SE Center for Photography as an exhibition and education venue after relocating from Maryland; he is represented in galleries across the United States and works regularly as an exhibition juror, curator, portfolio reviewer and speaker on the business of fine art photography. Between forty and fifty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $5 per image and you may submit up to fifteen. Membership is bought directly from the Center and is not itself juried: $25 a year for secondary-school and college students and educators of any age, $50 for over-60s, $60 for everyone else, with couple and supporter tiers above that; it also brings discounts on the Center's other calls and workshops. Images exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years are not eligible. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions close 6 November 2026, selections are announced 15 November, and the exhibition runs 1 December 2026 to 31 January 2027. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $5 per image (membership from $25/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — Black, White & More
item.description: The SE Center's open call on monochrome — images produced with a single hue rather than recording the colours of the thing photographed. The Center is looking for all forms of monochrome imagery, black-and-white and toned photography alike, any subject, analog, digital or antique processes, and photographers of every skill level and location may enter. The juror is Jennifer Schlesinger, an artist, curator, gallerist and educator based in Santa Fe whose own practice runs through the historical development of photography as an artistic medium — from the camera obscura to the nineteenth-century albumen process to twentieth-century gelatin silver printing, which along with albumen are her chosen mediums; her work mostly concerns landscape and how humans interact philosophically with the natural world. Between thirty-five and forty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $35 for up to five images and $6 for each additional image to a maximum of fifteen; members pay $28 and $5. Work exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years is not eligible, and there are no refunds for images not selected. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions opened 16 September 2026 and close 1 December; selections are announced 15 December and the exhibition opens 9 January 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portals · Collage Artists of America
item.description: Collage Artists of America, a Los Angeles society founded in 1988, opens its annual juried exhibition to members and non-members alike on the theme of portals. The organisers ask you to explore what defines a portal and to imagine one that resonates: an elaborate doorway leading to the known or the unknown, an opening into other universes or into the body or mind, any entrance to something real or imagined. Four kinds of work qualify — collage (flat or very low relief), mixed-media collage (moderate relief and/or different techniques and materials), assemblage (highly dimensional, multiple three-dimensional elements and/or freestanding) and digital collage, which the organisers define as a combination of multiple images and explicitly distinguish from digital manipulation of a single image, which does not qualify. For photographers that is the boundary to note: the prospectus never uses the word photograph in either direction, so the way in is the digital-collage definition itself - a photomontage is a combination of multiple images and qualifies, while a single unaltered frame does not. Nothing on any surface bars photographic material, and because the show is virtual there is no print or framing rule to fall foul of. The juror is Karin Skiba, who took her MFA at Claremont Graduate University, taught as a full-time art professor at Norco College and retired as Professor Emeritus, founded and directed the Norco College Art Gallery, was the inaugural director of the Hi-Desert Art Gallery and has curated at Joshua Tree's Juniper Arts Gallery. Awards total $1,300: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third, a $100 Carolann Watterson Memorial Award and up to four honourable mentions of $50 each. Entry is $40 for one work and $5 for each of up to three additional works for non-members, or $35 for up to four works for members; membership costs $55 and the entry maximum is four works either way. Work shown at any prior juried CAA exhibit is ineligible, as is work made in an instructor-directed, step-by-step class or workshop, and artificially generated artwork is not accepted. The exhibition is virtual only, hosted on the CAA website and on OnlineJuriedShows, and runs 1 November to 31 December 2026 with an online reception and awards on 1 November. CAA takes no commission on sales. Entries close 1 October 2026 at 11:59 PT and the jury's decisions are announced on 12 October. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 image + $5 each additional ($35/4 members). Prize: $1,300 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Draw the Line · Museum of Northern California Art
item.description: The Museum of Northern California Art in Chico invites artists to submit work for Draw the Line, a juried exhibition showcasing drawings of all kinds. The museum leans deliberately into a broad definition: it is seeking work where mark-making, line and gesture are the primary language, made with traditional and non-traditional tools on conventional and unconventional surfaces, including digital line work and three-dimensional material 'drawn' in a way that blurs the boundary between drawing and sculpture. The accepted-media line is 'All media', with one exclusion: no giclée prints of original art or non-photographic art will be accepted — a bar on reproductions rather than on photographs, and nothing on any surface excludes photographic or lens-based work. Photographers should read the theme honestly, though: this is a drawing show, and the work has to speak the language of line. Eligibility is regional — original work by artists residing in Northern California, which the museum defines as a named list of 41 counties from Del Norte and Siskiyou down to San Mateo, Santa Clara, Merced and Mariposa. Selection is made by the museum's exhibition committee of professional artists and art collectors. Entry through the museum's own form is $35 for up to three works, $25 for monca members, and $10 for each additional piece; entering instead through CaFÉ, where the museum keeps a parallel listing, prices the first image at $15 with $10 for each additional image to a maximum of eight, so a single entry is cheaper by that route while three works cost $35 either way. Fees are non-refundable and there is no refund if the work is not accepted. AI work and work previously exhibited at monca will be disqualified. Accepted work must arrive ready to hang, fitted with framing wire because the museum hangs from a picture rail — sawtooth hangers are disqualified — and must stay up until the exhibition closes. Sales carry a 50 percent museum commission, and shipping, packaging and insurance are the artist's responsibility. Entries and payment close 4 October 2026 at 5pm, the jury notifies by email on or before 18 October, and the exhibition runs 19 November 2026 to 10 January 2027 with a reception on 20 November. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $35/3 images ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Flora & Fauna · South x Southeast Photo Gallery
item.description: South x Southeast's Flora & Fauna is curated by gallery director Nancy McCrary and framed by E. O. Wilson's line that we should preserve every scrap of biodiversity as priceless while we learn to use it and come to understand what it means to humanity — Wilson being the American biologist and naturalist often called Darwin's natural heir. The call sets no further brief than the title, and the gallery illustrates it with two of McCrary's own pictures: tick weed and water lilies in the Okefenokee Swamp in late winter, and early morning in the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya. Selected photographs hang in the SxSE Gallery through November and December 2026 — a virtual gallery whose own tagline is "making the virtual a reality" — and a Zoom group review is held with the exhibiting photographers during that run, on a date to be announced. Entry is by email to the gallery director: images should be JPEG only, 72dpi and 1000 pixels on the longest side, named lastname-firstname-title (the gallery's own example is mccrarynancybigredhouse), zipped into a single file and attached to an email with the subject line "Flora & Fauna". The entry fee is $40 for the first four images and $10 for each additional image, paid separately through the gallery's shop. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $40 for 4 images; $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Dear Fear: An Anthology
item.description: Dear Fear is an anthology of letters written to "fear foods" — the foods and drinks that trigger intense anxiety, guilt, panic or distress — by people in eating disorder recovery, with images by contributing visual artists set alongside poems, essays and other creative nonfiction. The editors chose the constrained form deliberately, merging the epistle with the apostrophe (an address to a non-living thing) to bring their writers' voices into the same room, where they can hear one another beyond the characteristics that culture says should divide them. The call welcomes emerging writers and artists and particularly encourages submissions from communities that have historically faced resistance to representation, including LGBT+, BIPOC and disabled communities; the editors also note the relative lack of literature by men about eating disorders and recovery, and hope to make space for those voices. Visual artists and makers of hybrid work may submit up to five images, as JPG/JPEG only, 1,200 pixels on the longest side, sRGB, named FirstName_LastName_1.jpg; prose and poetry are submitted through Duotrope and visual work through a Google form that requires signing in to a Google account. Be aware that the organisers enumerate no media at all — the category is simply "Visual Art and Hybrid Work", and the word photograph appears nowhere on the submission page, the anthology's own Duotrope listing or the rest of the site; nothing excludes photography either, and the file specification admits it. What signals the visual intent is the masthead: the visual editor is Roula Seikaly, described on the anthology's own site as an independent curator, writer and Co-Director at Humble Arts Foundation whose curatorial practice addresses contemporary photography and new media, and who has curated exhibitions at SF Camerawork, Blue Sky Gallery, Colorado Photographic Arts Center and Photographic Center Northwest. The poetry editor is Danielle Coffyn and the nonfiction editor is Maggie Russell. Hybrid works involving video, music or other streaming content are not accepted at this time, and material generated by artificial intelligence cannot be accepted. Previously published work is ineligible, though the editors do not count work posted on a platform you control — a personal blog, newsletter or social account — as published; simultaneous submissions are welcome with prompt notice if the work is taken elsewhere. The submission fee is $3 and is waived on request, and optional editorial feedback from the editors costs $30; all fees go towards paying contributors, and accepted work receives what the editors call a modest honorarium, which they do not quantify. They aim to respond within three months, and will make accommodations for submissions from justice-involved or unhoused writers and artists, and from people submitting on their behalf. The submission window runs 1 August to 15 October 2026, and the anthology is anticipated to publish in February 2027 with Sheila-Na-Gig, a nonprofit poetry journal and small press. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $3 (waived on request). Prize: Publication + cash honorarium.

item.title: Conservation · Black Eyes Gallery
item.description: Black Eyes Gallery's second call asks a single question — what would you save? Conservation wants photographs of the land, buildings, species and traditions the photographer most wants still to be there in the future: cottonwoods on the U.S.–Mexico border that have stood two hundred years, acres of the Amazon already gone, plants and animals lost daily and mostly never photographed, buildings pulled down faster than anyone can record them, people threatened with destruction. The gallery's framing is that a photograph outlasts what it points at, and that the record is the one form of keeping available to almost anyone. Any genre is welcome so long as the work is photographic or lens based, and anything created entirely or substantially with artificial intelligence is disqualified. Twenty-five images are selected by juror Douglas Fur, a nationally exhibited Tucson photographer with a 2006 BFA from Cornish College of the Arts who spent two years at Decode Gallery and is now Artist Liaison and Gallery Manager for Tucson Erotica. Selected photographers send a file and nothing else: the gallery prints, mats and frames every accepted image at its own expense for the show at 485 S. Stone from 3 to 28 November 2026, then holds the single exhibition print in its archive for two years before destroying it. Accepted work also enters a permanent online archive carrying the artist's name, image title and social link, and is promoted across the gallery's social channels, email list and website with an individual feature on the Black Eyes Instagram. Entry is $40 for up to five images or $50 for up to ten; a reduced $20 fee is held for two artists per call on a first-come, first-served basis for anyone who writes in before submitting, and any entry that produces no selection earns $5 off the next one. Submissions are reviewed blind where possible, on creativity, originality, interpretation of the theme and how an image works against the exhibition as a whole, with CV and bio largely set aside. Work may optionally be offered for sale at a price the artist sets, the gallery retaining 50 per cent, and photographers keep full copyright throughout. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $50/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solo & Small Group Exhibition Proposals · K Space Contemporary
item.description: K Space Contemporary is a 501(c)(3) non-profit in downtown Corpus Christi dedicated to presenting contemporary art in South Texas, and its exhibition committee reviews artist portfolios once a year to fill solo and small-group slots across four spaces — the Clower Gallery (29' x 22'), the Starr Gallery (50' x 30'), the Corner Spot (16' x 23') and the Project Space (11.5' x 14.5'). The annual application deadline is 1 February. All media are accepted, including site-specific and immersive installation, and applicants choose a gallery preference and an exhibition category of 2-dimensional, 3-dimensional, installation/immersive or mixed. The gallery is looking for original, innovative work not previously exhibited at K Space. There is no cost to apply, and submission is by digital portfolio only: an artist website or a link to a Google Drive or Dropbox folder set to "anyone with the link" so the committee can review it, plus a written exhibition proposal. The gallery asks for images of at least ten different works, with an artist statement, biography and CV. Applicants must be 18 or older; entry is open to Texas artists, with particular interest in those living in the Texas Coastal Bend and South Texas. One application per artist per year is allowed. Submissions are accepted year round but reviewed only once, in spring, so an application filed shortly after a review waits ten to twelve months for an answer. Selected exhibitions are scheduled six to eighteen months in advance and run four to seven weeks; artists are responsible for delivering or shipping their own work and for installation and de-installation during gallery hours. K Space handles publicity — a press release to local and state media, an exhibition page on its site, an email invitation to around 2,000 subscribers, social promotion and 1,000 to 2,000 printed postcard announcements — and retains 40 per cent commission on gallery sales. Work must be collected or shipped out within ten days of the close; anything left 60 days after the last day becomes gallery property. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Athenaeum Solo or Group Show 2026–2027 · Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association
item.description: The Athenaeum Gallery, a Greek Revival landmark on Prince Street in Old Town Alexandria run by the Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association, sets aside part of its programme — an average of eight shows a year — for exhibitions proposed by artists and curators rather than chosen by the gallery director. This is the 2026–2027 review window, the successor to the cycle that closes on 30 September 2026: the portal opens the same day and accepts proposals through 30 September 2027, and the gallery describes the review as rolling rather than batched. Artists living or working in Virginia, Maryland or the District of Columbia may propose a solo show; a group of artists from the region may propose a group show; and a curator based anywhere may propose a show of work by artists from the area. Proposals are evaluated by gallery director Twig Murray on what the artist is trying to achieve or communicate, what makes the work distinctive, technical quality, and how recently the artist or the work has been shown locally. All visual media are welcome, photography included, but every work must be wall-mounted, less than nine inches deep and framed or fully finished, wired and ready to hang on picture hooks; nothing floor-mounted or free-standing is considered, and work requiring electricity is excluded. Sculpture may be entered only if it is under nine inches deep and lighter than 30 pounds. An application takes six to twelve images and up to three proposals per applicant are allowed. The artist, group or curator is responsible for getting work to the gallery and for collecting unsold work at the close. The Athenaeum insures everything in the show for the full retail price for the run, takes 40 per cent commission on sales and pays the artist within thirty days of closing; a curator-proposed show can negotiate a different split. Work does not have to be for sale to be included. Founded in 1964, the NVFAA is a registered 501(c)(3) supported by donations, member contributions, building rentals and sales commissions. — Deadline: September 30, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Inspired Annapolis · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County has given Maryland Federation of Art a show at the Annapolis Visitor's Center at 26 West Street in Historic Annapolis, a recently relaid space that around 800 people walk through every week, and MFA is filling it from this call.
